# Differential test harness — how to write a test

Read this before adding a test file.  `tests/write_read.rs` is the canonical
example; `tests/smoke.rs` is the smallest one.

## Ground rules

* The **C code in `c_src/` is the ground truth and must never be modified.**
  If C and Rust disagree, the Rust translation in `src/` is wrong.
* Never call a Rust function directly.  Everything goes through
  `common::Api`, whose fields are function pointers resolved with
  `libloading` from the two `.so`s.  This exercises the `#[no_mangle]`
  wrappers.
* Build and run with `./check.sh --test <name>` (it rebuilds the C `.so`, the
  Rust cdylib and the setjmp shim first — plain `cargo test` may silently test
  a stale `.so`).

## Skeleton

```rust
mod common;
use common::*;

#[test]
fn my_case() {
    assert_same("human readable case name", |api| unsafe {
        let mut o = Outcome::default();
        let (png, info) = new_write(api);           // or new_read(api)
        (api.png_set_write_fn)(png, core::ptr::null_mut(),
                               Some(write_cb), Some(flush_cb));
        let g = guarded(api, png, &mut || {
            // ... drive libpng here; png_error() longjmps back out of
            //     `guarded`, which returns Guard::Error(msg)
            (api.png_set_IHDR)(png, info, 4, 4, 8, PNG_COLOR_TYPE_RGB,
                               PNG_INTERLACE_NONE, PNG_COMPRESSION_TYPE_BASE,
                               PNG_FILTER_TYPE_BASE);
            (api.png_write_info)(png, info);
            (api.png_write_end)(png, info);
        });
        o.push(format!("guard={:?}", g));            // record the outcome
        o.output = std::mem::take(&mut tls().output); // and the bytes written
        destroy_write(api, png, info);
        o
    });
}
```

`assert_same` runs the closure **twice** — once with the C `Api`, once with the
Rust `Api`, each with a fresh `Tls` — and asserts that

1. the ordered event trace is identical, and
2. `Outcome::output` is byte-identical.

It panics with a readable diff of the first difference.  It also fails if a
scenario recorded *nothing* (which would mean the test does not exercise
anything).

## What to record

Anything the library tells you.  Cheap and effective:

* `log("...")` — appends to the trace from anywhere, including from a callback.
  Prefer `log` over `o.push` when ordering relative to callbacks matters.
* `o.push("...")` — appended after all callback events.
* `o.output` — the bytes to compare (written file, decoded rows, …).
* Return values, out-parameters, `png_get_*` results, `Guard`, warning text.

**Record aggressively.** A value you do not record cannot diverge visibly.

## Available pieces (`tests/common/`)

| item | what it is |
|------|-----------|
| `libs()` | `&'static Libs { c: Api, rust: Api, shim: Shim }` |
| `Api` | one field per exported symbol — **all 384** of them, generated by `tools/gen_api.py` from `png.h` + `pngpriv.h`.  `grep '<name>' tests/common/api.rs` to see a signature. |
| `guarded(api, png, &mut || {...}) -> Guard` | arms libpng's error trap; `Guard::Ok` / `Guard::Error(String)` / `Guard::NoTrap` |
| `new_read` / `new_write` / `destroy_read` / `destroy_write` | create/destroy with the harness error+warning handlers installed |
| `read_cb` / `write_cb` / `flush_cb` | memory IO callbacks; input in `tls().input`, output in `tls().output` |
| `read_status_cb` / `write_status_cb` | row/pass callbacks that log |
| `user_transform_cb` | a deterministic user transform that logs and mangles the row |
| `malloc_cb` / `free_cb` | a logging allocator for `png_set_mem_fn` |
| `tls()` | per-thread `Tls { trace, input, in_pos, output, flushes, rows, counter, allocs, .. }` |
| `Rng::new(seed)` | SplitMix64: `u32() u8() below(n) range(lo,hi) bytes(n) pick(&[..]) bool()` |
| `Img::random(rng, w, h, ct, bd)` | a random image of a legal shape (+ palette) |
| `write_image` / `write_plain` / `WriteOpts` | drive a whole write; `extra` hook runs between `png_set_IHDR` and `png_write_info` |
| `read_image` / `read_plain` / `ReadOpts` / `RowMode` | drive a whole read; `setup` hook runs right after `png_read_info` |
| `log_info(api, png, info, tag)` | dump the whole IHDR/rowbytes/valid state |
| `chunk(name, data)` / `chunk_bad_crc` / `insert_before` / `insert_after_last` / `split_chunks` / `crc32` / `SIG` | build or patch a PNG datastream by hand |
| `VALID_SHAPES` | the 15 legal `(color_type, bit_depth)` pairs |
| `PNG_*` constants | in `common::types` |

## Gotchas

* `png_error` never returns — it `longjmp`s out of `guarded`.  Anything after
  the failing call inside the `guarded` body is skipped, in **both** libraries,
  which is exactly what we want to compare.
* After `Guard::Error` the `png_struct` may only be destroyed.
* Keep buffers alive across the call (`let v = ...; (api.f)(v.as_ptr())`) —
  a temporary would dangle.
* `png_read_row` needs `rowbytes` **after** `png_read_update_info`, which can
  grow the row (expand, gray→rgb, filler, …).
* Seed every `Rng` from a constant so failures reproduce.
* Use many randomised inputs per configuration — one hand-picked value per
  configuration is not enough.
